summary: sitecard exposes an interactive SSH shell on the installer's host through a public tunnel
details: sitecard advertises itself as a tool to issue temporary SSH access cards. When the user runs the CLI subcommand, it starts a loopback asyncssh gateway (bound to 127.0.0.1) that spawns a child process with a PTY and bridges SSH input/output into it (launch_gateway spawns 'python -m sitecard.gateway'; pump_ssh_input writes received SSH bytes to the child's stdin/PTY). The gateway is then exposed to the public internet via a configurable reverse-tunnel transport, defaulting to srv.us (SITECARD_TUNNEL_HOST), with options for upterm, cloudflare/cloudflared, devtunnel, and a ws-relay. By default sessions are public/no-auth ('--accept'); key-based authentication is opt-in via '--no-public-access'. The capability is disclosed in the README and only fires when the operator invokes the foreground subcommand — the package's pyproject uses plain setuptools with no install hooks, and __init__ only sets a version string, so nothing starts on install or import. The resulting surface is a full interactive shell on the operator's workspace reachable by anyone who learns the tunnel URL while public mode is active, with blast radius equal to the invoking user's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
